title: Implement interactive installation wizard
outOfScope: Changing the existing installer transaction, branch, rollback, or Work Item creation logic.
Changing the Work Item 4 IO and localization primitives.
Entrypoint routing, calibration behavior, recovery UX, release publication, and third-party dependencies.

sources.reason: Defines the eight-step wizard behavior and boundaries.
Existing installer transaction to reuse after confirmation.
Read-only repository and stack detection APIs from the predecessor Work Item.

riskAssessment.reason: The wizard must remain read-only until explicit confirmation while presenting deterministic facts and delegating the confirmed transaction to the existing installer.

executionDecision.reason: The wizard scope, evidence, risks, scenarios, and verification gates are defined.

preReviewWarnings: Review that no target repository write occurs before final confirmation.
Review that all eight steps render the required explanation and checklist fields.
Review that confirmation delegates to the existing installer without adding commit, push, PR, or merge automation.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: The wizard exposes exactly eight ordered steps: Target Repository, Repository Readiness, Installation Mode, Project Stack, Installation Options, Adoption Branch, Installation Plan Review, and Installation/Result.
Before final confirmation, the wizard performs only read-only target inspection, renders facts and a complete plan, and states no-commit/no-push/no-PR/no-merge behavior; Dry Run remains read-only.

The wizard presents New Adoption, Upgrade, and Dry Run choices and captures iOS Swift Package, Xcode project, CocoaPods, Android modules/flavors/variants/JDK/test signals, Generic, and multi-stack facts; an Xcode layout fixture covers the multi-project case.
After explicit confirmation, the wizard reuses the existing installer transaction and protects conflict files; tests assert no writes before confirmation and the specified post-confirmation result.
Public APIs have docstrings and the scripted interaction contract is covered by focused tests; all repository governance checks pass.
guidelines: Reuse the existing installer transaction after confirmation; do not duplicate transaction, branch, rollback, or Work Item creation logic.
Do not write to the target repository before explicit final confirmation; transient recovery may use only a system temp directory.
Use standard-library APIs and injectable argument lists so scripted and non-TTY tests are deterministic.
Document public APIs and keep the wizard limited to this Work Item's eight-step orchestration.

intent.problem: The installer has reusable detection and transaction primitives, but users need a guided, reviewable installation flow that explains repository facts, choices, impact, and the exact write boundary before anything changes.
constraints: The eight steps and their order are fixed by the plan.
Target inspection is read-only until final confirmation, and no commit, push, PR, or merge is automated by the wizard.
The implementation must reuse the existing installer transaction and remain compatible with non-TTY scripted execution.
intent.rationale: Separating presentation and planning from the existing transaction makes the confirmation boundary testable and keeps installation behavior governed by one implementation.

rawUserRequest: 循环执行 docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-25-interactive-installation-calibration-wizard.md 的全部工单流程，中途不要停止；如需授权视为已授权，直到全部完成。

scenarioCoverage.expected: All target reads complete and the full plan is shown before any target write; cancel exits without mutation.
Exactly eight fixed steps render in order, with deterministic back/cancel behavior and a final checklist.
Confirmed non-dry-run delegates to the existing installer and preserves conflict files.
Dry Run performs no target write and represents iOS, Android, Generic, and multi-stack facts/options.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: User explicitly authorized completion of the full governed workflow.
